skill.name: prototype
skill.description: Build three to five distinct UI variants in an isolated visual picker, compare their tradeoffs, and promote the selected design.
skill.summary: Explore distinct UI directions in a live picker before integrating a chosen variant.
skill.author: emilkowalski

content.value_statement: Choosing a UI direction from one implementation limits useful comparison. This skill builds distinct, working variants in a live picker before integration.
actual_capabilities: Scopes each run to one UI component or interaction.
Reviews the project stack, design tokens, personality, and rendering context.
Builds three distinct variants by default, with a maximum of five.
Creates an isolated route or standalone HTML picker for live comparison.
Verifies rendering and interactions, then presents each direction with its tradeoff.
Integrates the selected variant and removes the prototype unless preservation is requested.
limitations: It explores one UI component per run, not an entire product interface.
It requires explicit invocation and waits for the user to select a variant.
It does not review existing UI quality or choose third-party dependencies.
Browser screenshots depend on available browser tooling.

use_cases.title: Compare Product UI Directions
use_cases.description: Explore distinct layouts and interaction models for a product component before committing engineering time.

use_cases.title: Prototype Within an Existing App
use_cases.description: Build isolated variants that reuse the current framework, tokens, and frontend conventions.

use_cases.title: Review a Decision With Stakeholders
use_cases.description: Present working alternatives in a consistent picker with clear benefits and costs.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Simple Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Prototype three distinct versions of a settings save button. Keep them consistent with this project and show them in the picker.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner exploration of one clear component

prompt_templates.title: Compare Interaction Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Prototype three notification center variants that differ in layout, density, and interaction model. Use realistic content and preserve accessibility.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused comparison across named design axes

prompt_templates.title: Expand the Design Space
prompt_templates.prompt: Prototype five checkout confirmation variants. Explore quiet, editorial, compact, reassuring, and action-focused directions within the existing design system.
prompt_templates.scenario: Broad exploration for an important product moment

prompt_templates.title: Refine and Promote a Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Riff on the compact variant with three new directions. After I choose one, integrate it and remove the prototype surface.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced iterative exploration and final integration

output: Guarded: explicit warning, typed confirmation, and restrained motion.
Progressive: consequences appear before the destructive action becomes available.
Contextual: account impact and export options sit beside the final action.

output_examples.output: The Dense variant is integrated using the project's existing conventions. The temporary prototype surface is removed.
A new picker presents three editorial variations with distinct hierarchy, spacing, and motion approaches.

best_practices: Describe one component, its product context, and its required interactions.
Name the design axes that matter, such as density, hierarchy, motion, or interaction model.
Compare every variant live before selecting one for integration.
anti_patterns: Do not request an entire dashboard or multi-page flow in one run.
Do not treat color-only changes as genuinely different design directions.
Do not promote a variant before checking its interactions and tradeoffs.

faq.question: How many variants does the skill create?
faq.answer: It creates three variants by default and supports up to five when requested.

faq.question: Does it modify production code immediately?
faq.answer: No. Exploration stays isolated until you explicitly select a variant for integration.

faq.question: Can it work without an existing project?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create a self-contained HTML prototype with inline styles and scripts.

faq.question: Does it use the existing design system?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews available tokens, frameworks, and conventions so variants fit the product.

faq.question: Can I request another round?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask it to riff on a named variant to generate new directions around that choice.

faq.question: What happens after I choose a variant?
faq.answer: It integrates the selected design and removes the prototype unless you ask to keep it.
